questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola with Vertex at the Origin Given Another Point
questions.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(-4,-6).$
questions.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(-4,-6),$ we can substitute $x=-4$ and $y=-6$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ (-6)^{2} & =4p(-4) \\ 36 & =-16p \\ p & =-\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(-\frac{9}{4})x \\ {y}^{2} & =-9x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13972835/assets/e4b681e9bdf5fa8021ca359e0bf93c27b53a18f0d5e906765a911a72ecfc0159.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the left. The parabola has its vertex at $(4,2)$ and passes through the point $(-8,10).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(4,2),$ we substitute $h=4$ and $k=2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(-8,10),$ so we can substitute $x=-8$ and $y=10$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x-4) \\ (10-2)^{2} & =4p(-8-4) \\ 64 & =-48p \\ p & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x-4) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =4(-\frac{4}{3})(x-4) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =-\frac{16}{3}(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the left since $p=-\frac{4}{3}$ is negative.

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the left. The parabola has its vertex at $(6,4)$ and passes through the point $(1,9).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(6,4),$ we substitute $h=6$ and $k=4$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-4)^{2} & =4p(x-6).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(1,9),$ so we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=9$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-4)^{2} & =4p(x-6) \\ (9-4)^{2} & =4p(1-6) \\ 25 & =-20p \\ p & =-\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-4)^{2} & =4p(x-6) \\ (y-4)^{2} & =4(-\frac{5}{4})(x-6) \\ (y-4)^{2} & =-5(x-6).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the left since $p=-\frac{5}{4}$ is negative.

questions.problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(0,2)$ and passes through the point $(5,5).$
questions.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(0,2),$ we substitute $h=0$ and $k=2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4px.\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(5,5),$ so we can substitute $x=5$ and $y=5$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4px \\ (5-2)^{2} & =4p(5) \\ 9 & =20p \\ p & =\frac{9}{20}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4px \\ (y-2)^{2} & =4(\frac{9}{20})x \\ (y-2)^{2} & =\frac{9}{5}x.\end{aligned}
$$
